knowledge_point.title: Differentiating a General Exponential Function Using the Chain Rule

question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we express $y$ as the composite function

$$
y=4\cdot {2}^{u},\,u=2x-3{x}^{3}.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}u}=4\cdot {2}^{u}\ln(2),\,\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=2-9{x}^{2}.
$$

We now apply the chain rule and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} & =\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}u}\cdot \frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x} \\ & =4\cdot {2}^{u}\ln(2)\cdot (2-9{x}^{2}) \\ & =(2-9{x}^{2})\cdot 4\cdot {2}^{u}\ln(2) \\ & =(8-36{x}^{2})\cdot {2}^{2x-3{x}^{3}}\ln(2).\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we express $y$ as the composite function

$$
y={5}^{u},\,u=-2x+{x}^{3}.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}u}={5}^{u}\ln(5),\,\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=-2+3{x}^{2}.
$$

We now apply the chain rule and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} & =\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}u}\cdot \frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x} \\ & ={5}^{u}\ln(5)\cdot (-2+3{x}^{2}) \\ & =(-2+3{x}^{2})\cdot {5}^{u}\ln(5) \\ & =(-2+3{x}^{2})\cdot {5}^{-2x+{x}^{3}}\ln(5).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the slope $m$ of the tangent to the curve at $x=-1$, we have to evaluate $\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$ at that point as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m=\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}\big|_{x=-1} & =(-2+3(-1)^{2})\cdot {5}^{-2(-1)+(-1)^{3}}\ln(5) \\ & =1\cdot {5}^{1}\ln(5) \\ & =5 \ln{\left(5 \right)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent to the curve at the point where $x=-1$ is $5 \ln{\left(5 \right)}.$

question.:question/problem: Find the slope $m$ of the tangent to the curve $y={4}^{-6x}$ at the point where $x=- \frac{1}{6}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we express $y$ as the composite function

$$
y={4}^{u},\,u=-6x.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}u}={4}^{u}\ln(4),\,\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=-6.
$$

We now apply the chain rule and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} & =\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}u}\cdot \frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x} \\ & ={4}^{u}\ln(4)\cdot (-6) \\ & =(-6)\cdot {4}^{u}\ln(4) \\ & =-6\cdot {4}^{-6x}\ln(4).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the slope $m$ of the tangent to the curve at $x=- \frac{1}{6}$, we have to evaluate $\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$ at that point as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m=\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}\big|_{x=- \frac{1}{6}} & =(-6)\cdot {4}^{-6(- \frac{1}{6})}\ln(4) \\ & =-6\cdot {4}^{1}\ln(4) \\ & =- 24 \ln{\left(4 \right)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent to the curve at the point where $x=- \frac{1}{6}$ is $- 24 \ln{\left(4 \right)}.$

question.:question/problem: Find the equation of the tangent to the curve $y={5}^{4x+3}$ at the point where $x=-1.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we express $y$ as the composite function

$$
y={5}^{u},\,u=4x+3.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}u}={5}^{u}\ln(5),\,\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=4.
$$

We now apply the chain rule and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} & =\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}u}\cdot \frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x} \\ & ={5}^{u}\ln(5)\cdot (4) \\ & =(4)\cdot {5}^{u}\ln(5) \\ & =4\cdot {5}^{4x+3}\ln(5).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the slope $m$ of the tangent to the curve at $x=-1$, we have to evaluate $\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$ at that point as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m=\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}\big|_{x=-1} & =(4)\cdot {5}^{4(-1)+3}\ln(5) \\ & =4\cdot {5}^{-1}\ln(5) \\ & =\frac{4 \ln{\left(5 \right)}}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent to the curve at the point where $x=-1$ is $\frac{4 \ln{\left(5 \right)}}{5}.$

Also, the $y$-value of the point on the curve where $x=-1$ is

$$
y_1={5}^{-1}=\frac{1}{5}.
$$

Finally, we find the equation of the tangent at that point:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-y_1&=m(x-x_1) \\ y-(\frac{1}{5})&=(\frac{4 \ln{\left(5 \right)}}{5})\left(x-(-1)\right) \\ y&=\frac{4 x \ln{\left(5 \right)}}{5} + \frac{1}{5} + \frac{4 \ln{\left(5 \right)}}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
